'''Dorothy Elizabeth Stahl Brady''' (June 14, 1903 – April 17, 1977) was an American [[mathematician]] and [[economist]]. She was a professor of economics at [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania]] from 1958 to 1970.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Richard A. |last=Easterlin |title=Dorothy Stahl Brady, 1903–1977 |journal=[[Journal of Economic History]] |volume=38 |issue=1 |year=1978 |pages=301–303 |jstor=2119341 |doi=10.1017/S0022050700088318 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life==
Born in [[Elk River, Minnesota]], she grew up in [[Portland, Oregon]], attending [[Lincoln High School (Portland, Oregon)|Lincoln High School]] and later [[Reed College]] studying mathematics and physics. She graduated from Reed in 1924.<ref>Reed College, [https://rdc.reed.edu/record/58358?ln=en&p=yearbooks&v=uv#?xywh=358%2C2136%2C1006%2C681&cv=13 ''The Griffin''] (1924 yearbook): 26.</ref> She was married to fellow Reed student [[Robert A. Brady (economist)|Robert A. Brady]] from 1924 to 1936, they had a son in 1933.<ref name=":0">{{cite book|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&pg=PA147|contribution=Brady, Dorothy (Stahl)|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhDs|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics|last1=Green|first1=Judy|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=2009|isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5|pages=147–48|author1-link=Judy Green (mathematician)|author2-link=Jeanne LaDuke}} See also pp. 11, 95. Biography on pp. 97–102 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

==Education and career==
Brady earned a master's degree in mathematics from [[Cornell University]] in 1926, then worked as an instructor at [[Vassar College]], as a research assistant at the [[National Bureau of Economic Research]], and a studied and taught at [[New York University]]. She went on to complete a Ph.D. in mathematics from [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1933, and was the 6th woman ever to do so.<ref name=":0" />

Brady went on to a long career in government working for the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]] and the [[U.S. Department of Labor]] where she was the chief of the cost of living division from 1944 to 1948, and the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] where she was the chief of division of prices and cost of living in 1953.

She returned to academia as a professor in 1956 at the [[University of Chicago]], was chairman of the graduate group in economic history from 1964 to 1970 at the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania|Wharton School]] of the [[University of Pennsylvania]].  She continued to consult to the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] and the [[Social Security Administration]] during her academic tenure.<ref name=":0" />

==Honors==
Brady received the [[National Woman's Press Association|National Women's Press Club]] Award in Economics, and was book review editor of the [[The Journal of Economic History|Journal of Economic History]] from 1969 to 1974.<ref name=":0" /> Brady became a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1949<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm List of ASA Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, retrieved 2016-07-16.</ref> and Fellow of the [[Econometric Society]] in 1950.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memory of Fellows of the Econometric Society |url=https://www.econometricsociety.org/society/organization-and-governance/fellows/memoriam |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=The Econometric Society |language=en}}</ref>
